Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees, roughly 27% of its workforce, including staff on teams building Copilot and other AI products, as the company looks for ways to fund its AI investments.

Amy Coleman, executive vice president and chief people officer, announced the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) in an internal memo on Monday, which Microsoft republished on its official blog.

title: Microsoft offers exits to thousands, including employees on AI and Copilot teams

description:
OpenAI has launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a new reasoning model that it says delivers near-frontier performance on visual reasoning, professional task execution, and computer-use benchmarks without the premium price tag. Replacing GPT-5.6 Terra, the model is aimed at organizations seeking better accuracy and automation capabilities for large-scale operational workloads.

Claiming it to be a step up from GPT-5.6 Terra at 50% lower price, OpenAI said its new mid-tier model is designed to handle everyday professional work such as drafting proposals, interpreting technical drawings, filling out forms, and editing videos.
title: OpenAI bets on AI economics with lower-cost GPT-6.1 Terra

description:
AI is getting expensive, and companies are looking to cut token costs. The solution: move more AI work to PCs.

The PC won’t replace the cloud. Preliminary AI work can be done on a PC, and tougher work — which today’s PCs can’t handle — can go to the cloud.

title: The right model at the right moment: Vendors push their agentic AI PC vision

When OpenAI’s GPT-3 was released in 2020, at 175 billion parameters, it was the largest language model the world had ever seen. In the years that followed, frontier AI systems exploded in size, with today’s largest models clocking in at well over a trillion parameters. But there is a countercurrent of AI research moving in the opposite direction, with pioneers like Tether building a new generation of smaller AI models.
